label: In act
resolution: The case does not choose between the two senses. Every premise that speaks of act (STMT-NOTHING-MOVES-EXCEPT-AS-IN-ACT, STMT-NOTHING-IN-ACT-AND-POTENCY-IN-SAME-RESPECT, STMT-PLURAL-FIRST-MOVERS-WOULD-DIFFER-IN-ACT, STMT-ACTUALITY-ONLY-INSOFAR-AS-BEING, STMT-FIRST-UNMOVED-MOVER-HAS-EVERY-PERFECTION) uses the one parameter `InAct`, so within a result every premise is read in the same sense and no step passes from one sense to the other. The choice matters for premise truth, not validity: read formally, 'a thing moves only as in act' faces causes that produce what they do not themselves have; read virtually, the non-simultaneity premise must hold for virtual act too. A defence of these premises must fix one sense and defend all of them in it. BRIDGE-ARIST-POTENCY-ANALYSIS-NON-SIMULTANEITY reads the Metaphysics IX.6 analysis (STMT-POTENCY-IS-UNACTUALIZED-CAPACITY) with the same `InAct` as the non-simultaneity premise, so no step changes sense. IX.6 says 'not actually r' of formal act; read virtually, the analysis would say that potency to r excludes virtual act of r, a stronger reading than IX.6 states. The bridge therefore carries Aristotle's support to the premise on the formal reading only. STMT-PERFECT-INSOFAR-AS-IN-ACT, through which AQUINAS-ST-I-Q5-A1-GOODNESS-FROM-DESIRABILITY derives STMT-GOODNESS-IS-ACTUALITY, uses the one parameter `Has` of the conclusion, which the case instantiates by `InAct`; so the goodness steps take whatever sense the other act premises of a result take. ST I q.4 a.1 co. and q.5 a.1 co. speak of a thing's own act, so their support is for the formal reading. In the owner-adopted configurations (#1007), DEF-POTENCY is defined using the very same supplied InAct predicate at every use, so ADOPTED-POTENCY-NONOVERLAP is analytic relative to F1 in that chosen sense. This does not establish that a historical passage uses the virtual analysis or that the framework inputs apply to reality. The general parameterized routes and their rival readings remain available under DISAMB-POTENCY. Sense fork (docs/notes/load-bearing-terms.md, TruthCore.Causality.TermSenseForks2): Senses are labelled IN-ACT_1 formal (DEF-IN-ACT-FORMALLY), IN-ACT_2 virtual (DEF-IN-ACT-VIRTUALLY) and IN-ACT_3 formal-or-virtual (DEF-IN-ACT-FORMALLY-OR-VIRTUALLY, added for the fork); ActSense enumerates them over the new parameters InActFormally and InActVirtually. The primary results are one argument per sense: NO-SELF-MOTION-SAME-RESPECT-IN-ACT-1, -2 and -3. Coverage (STMT-IN-ACT-SENSES-EXHAUSTIVE) and exclusivity of the route's reading (STMT-IN-ACT-SENSE-UNIQUE) are OPEN frontier premises. The optional summary IN-ACT-SENSE-FORK-NO-SELF-MOTION reaches STMT-NOTHING-MOVES-ITSELF-IN-SAME-RESPECT whichever single sense both uses take; the controls show the mixed reading (mover virtually in act, non-simultaneity formal) allows self-motion, which certifies the equivocation risk described above. Strength order: the formal mover premise strengthens the inclusive one, and inclusive non-simultaneity strengthens the formal one, so no uniform reading is weaker in both premises.
